question: What is the name of the suture that separates the two parietal bones along the top of the fetal head?
explanation: The sagittal suture runs right along the midline at the top of the head, dividing the left and right parietal bones. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h1)

question: Why are the bones of the fetal skull separated by sutures and fontanelles during childbirth?

options.A: To prevent the cerebrospinal fluid from building up inside the cranial cavity
options.B: To allow the skull bones to overlap and change shape inside the pelvis
options.C: To protect the baby's brain from normal changes in maternal blood pressure
options.D: To provide extra room for rapid brain growth during the first stage of labour

explanation: The gaps in the skull allow the bones to shift and overlap, reducing the head's diameter so it can pass safely through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h1)

question: What is moulding in the context of labour?

options.A: The stretching of the lower uterine segment during the second stage of labour
options.B: The natural softening of the cervix before active contractions begin
options.C: The abnormal swelling of the baby's scalp caused by pressure
options.D: The shifting and overlapping of fetal skull bones to fit through the pelvis

explanation: Moulding is the medical term for the overlapping of the baby's skull plates to reduce head size during birth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h2)

question: What happens to the fetal skull bones after the baby is delivered and moulding is no longer needed?

options.A: They remain permanently overlapped until the child reaches toddler age
options.B: They fuse together immediately to protect the brain from outside injury
options.C: They gradually return to their normal shape as the pressure is relieved
options.D: They separate permanently and require surgical correction in the nursery

explanation: Because the skull bones are flexible and joined by elastic tissue, the head regains its normal rounded appearance shortly after birth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h2)

question: Which grade of moulding describes skull bones that overlap firmly but can still be separated by finger pressure?
explanation: Grade 1 means the bones overlap slightly but remain reducible with gentle pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h3)

question: During a vaginal exam, a student midwife feels the baby's skull bones overlapping tightly with no way to separate them. How is this charted?
explanation: When bones overlap firmly and won't budge, that's advanced moulding (Grade 2 or 3). It's a key sign to watch out for to prevent prolonged or blocked labour!

question: What is the primary purpose of recording moulding on the partograph during labour?

options.A: To measure the strength and frequency of maternal uterine contractions
options.B: To detect early signs of mechanical obstruction or tight pelvis
options.C: To determine the exact volume of amniotic fluid remaining in the uterus
options.D: To calculate the exact gestational age of the fetus before delivery

explanation: Moulding is tracked on the partograph primarily to catch signs of difficult labour and cephalopelvic disproportion early. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h4)

question: Why do midwives check both cervical dilation and moulding together on the partograph?

options.A: Cervical dilation causes the skull bones to separate rather than overlap
options.B: A baby may have a normal cervix opening while the head remains stuck due to poor fit
options.C: Good moulding always guarantees that the baby will be delivered within one hour
options.D: Moulding only occurs during the third stage of active labour after the cervix is fully open

explanation: Looking at both helps you see the whole picture. Sometimes the cervix opens up nicely, but the baby's head isn't actually moving down because of a tight fit!

question: What is caput succedaneum?

options.A: Bleeding underneath the tough skull bone covering called the periosteum
options.B: Swelling of the scalp soft tissues caused by pressure from the cervix
options.C: The abnormal upward displacement of the anterior fontanelle
options.D: Permanent fusion of the cranial sutures before the baby is born

explanation: Caput is a localized edema or swelling of the baby's scalp that occurs because of pressure from the cervix during labour. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h5)

question: How can a nurse tell the difference between moulding and caput succedaneum during a physical assessment?

options.A: Caput only happens in breech presentations, while moulding only happens in head-first births
options.B: Moulding disappears within minutes of birth, but caput lasts for several months
options.C: Moulding involves bone overlapping, whereas caput is soft swelling that can cross over suture lines
options.D: Caput feels hard like solid bone, whereas moulding feels soft like fluid

explanation: Caput is soft fluid swelling that crosses suture lines, while moulding is the shifting of the hard skull bones themselves. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h5)

question: What serious condition is strongly suspected when you see severe, locked Grade 3 moulding during labour?
explanation: Grade 3 moulding means the bones are tightly locked and won't budge. That's a major red flag telling us the labour is blocked.

question: A patient in labour shows severe moulding and the baby's heart rate is dropping. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the mother to push harder with every contraction to speed up birth
options.B: Wait another two hours to see if the cervix dilates any further on its own
options.C: Administer oxytocin infusion to strengthen contractions and force descent
options.D: Notify the doctor immediately and prepare for an emergency Caesarean section

explanation: When severe moulding meets a distressed baby heart rate, time is precious! Call the doctor right away and get ready for an emergency CS to save the day.

question: What is the most important thing a nurse should do when abnormal moulding shows up on the partograph?

options.A: Document the finding and wait until the end of the shift to report it
options.B: Report the finding promptly to the doctor or senior midwife
options.C: Perform an operative vaginal delivery without waiting for assistance
options.D: Restrict all oral fluids to prevent further swelling of the head

explanation: Never keep dangerous findings to yourself! Speak up and report worsening signs like severe moulding right away so the team can jump into action.

question: Why is it so vital to write down moulding details accurately on the partograph?

options.A: It proves that the nurse gave pain medication at the correct time
options.B: It replaces the need to check the fetal heart rate during the second stage
options.C: It serves as a legal receipt for the hospital fees charged to the patient
options.D: It gives the healthcare team a clear visual trend of whether labour is becoming obstructed

explanation: The partograph gives everyone a quick visual story of how labour is going, helping the whole shift spot dangerous trends before they become emergencies.
